question: How can the prefill and decode phases and the KV cache be tuned beyond high-level disaggregation, through decode kernels, KV pooling and reuse, fast KV transfer, per-phase hardware and parallelism, and adaptive scheduling?
contributions: Survey of decode kernels (FlashMLA, ThunderMLA, FlexDecoding), KV pooling/prefix reuse, zero-copy KV transfer, heterogeneous per-phase hardware/parallelism, SLO-aware admission and adaptive scaling.

results.quote: LMCache reports ~20 ms → ~8 ms for a 7.5k-token KV after collation on RDMA.
results.note: Also stated as 'about 20 milliseconds ... about 8 milliseconds' later in the section.

limits: Most numbers are reported from other work (Splitwise, HexGen-2, Arrow, ThunderMLA, POD-Attention, LMCache) with little setup; no experiments of its own.
Parallelism tables are labelled illustrative values.
FP4 support is described as still maturing; chapter is time-stamped to its writing.
KV-size worked example ignores GQA/MQA, which would shrink real 70B KV sizes.
Hardware for the ThunderMLA and POD-Attention figures and baselines are not stated.
practices: Evaluate FlashMLA to raise per-token decode throughput without changing higher-level architecture (FlashMLA).
Prefer torch.compile(mode="max-autotune") for stable latency-critical decode, with a narrow capture boundary (FlexDecoding).
Prefer the PyTorch NJT layout for ragged batching during decode (FlexDecoding).
Prefer Transformer Engine FP8 (MXFP8) for prefill and decode; consider NVFP4 only when accuracy permits (FlexDecoding).
Treat the KV cache as a first-class shared resource: pool it across GPUs/CPU/NVMe and reuse prefixes by hash (Tuning KV Cache).
Use exact-prefix caching with LRU-style eviction; route requests to the node that holds their prefix (KV Cache Reuse).
Keep active KV in GPU HBM for latency-critical decode and use Grace LPDDR5X only as a lower tier (Superchip section).
Use GPUDirect RDMA/NIXL zero-copy transfer, overlapped on a dedicated CUDA stream, and verify overlap with Nsight Systems (Fast KV Cache Transfer).
Collate KV pages to >=128-token pages per RDMA write; collate 16-token pages into >=128-token slabs (Fast KV Cache Transfer).
Size pd_buffer_size from 2 x L x N x (H x Dh) x bytes_per_val, start at 1 GB, round up to 256 MB, shrink proportionally for FP8/FP4 KV (Fast KV Cache Transfer).
Enable CUDA IPC on a single node and RDMA across nodes; set UCX_RNDV_THRESH=16384 and validate with ucx_info -f (Fast KV Cache Transfer).
Set PYTHONHASHSEED=0 for deterministic KV-chunk routing in multiprocess runs (Fast KV Cache Transfer).
Benchmark global-queue vs per-request direct-channel connectors under the expected request mix (Connector and Data Path Design).
Use compute-rich GPUs for prefill and memory-bandwidth-rich, cheaper GPUs for decode (Heterogeneous Hardware).
Run prefill with high TP/PP and decode with TP_d=1 by default, raising TP_d only if the model does not fit; avoid PP for decode (Tables 18-1, 18-2).
Route very long or low-priority prompts to CPU prefill workers only as a safety net, monitor how often, and fail fast over SLO (Hybrid Prefill).
Apply early rejection/admission control and reserve capacity per QoS tier (e.g. 10% premium, 30% standard) (SLO-Aware Request Management).
Monitor prefill/decode queues and TTFT/TPOT p99 and p99.9 separately, and enforce a minimum role dwell time to avoid flip oscillation (Dynamic Scheduling).

terms.definition: An optimized decoding kernel from DeepSeek focused on the single-token decode step, fusing operations and using the GPU memory hierarchy better.
A completely fused attention decode megakernel from Stanford that focuses on decoding and scheduling, reducing launch overhead and tail effects.
The decoding backend of torch.nn.attention.flex_attention; compiles a specialised kernel for Q_len=1 over a growing KV cache.
Decouples KV storage from individual GPUs, spreading it across cluster GPU memory with CPU DRAM and NVMe as overflow.
SM-aware CTA scheduling that binds each CTA at runtime to a prefill or decode task so both share an SM in one fused kernel.
NVIDIA Inference Xfer Library, a plugin-based library for zero-copy GPU-to-GPU and GPU-to-storage transfer.
Admission control that fails fast when the system predicts it cannot serve a request within its latency target.
TetriInfer mechanism in which nodes switch between prefill and decode roles.
